entertainment.title: ‘Red Before Dawn’ Review: A Road Movie Revisits the Indonesian Revolution in Ways More Didactic Than Climactic
entertainment.summary: Garin Nugroho’s wartime drama follows a group of disparate characters dangerously making their way across Indonesia as the fight for independence rages on.
entertainment.body:
Few people outside of Indonesia are likely to be familiar with the war of independence that began there just as WWII was coming to an end, resulting in hundreds of thousands of deaths at the hands of both Dutch soldiers and warring sectarian factions. The country finally achieved full emancipation from the Netherlands in 1949, though the wounds opened by the long and often brutal conflict would remain for the decades that followed.

Prolific Indonesian director Garin Nugroho revisits that pivotal historical period in Red Before Dawn ( Merah Sebelum Fajar ), a wartime road movie that condenses multiple aspects of the revolution into one rocky and dangerous trip through hostile territory. Following a cast of diverse characters who journey from Jakarta to Yogyakarta in 1946, facing countless obstacles but growing closer along the way, the film attempts to show how people from various ethnic and religious backgrounds managed to finally unite behind a single flag. Related Stories Business Tokyo: Industry Insiders Skeptical of Bold Japanese Government Plans for Overseas Content Sales Push Business Tokyo: Japan's New Production Incentives Risk Doing as Much Harm as Good Red Before Dawn The Bottom Line Historically intriguing but dramatically lacking. Venues: Tokyo International Film Festival Cast: Nicholas Saputra, Laura Basuki, Bront Palarae, Tissa Biani, Nagra Pakesadewo, Mariska Setiawan Director, producer: Garin Nugroho Screenwriters: Garin Nugroho, Dirmawan Hatta 1 hour 53 minutes

On paper the idea is intriguing, and Red Before Dawn benefits from both an ambitious set-up and a highly cinematic setting, traveling through lush jungles and fields, rivers, villages and ancient ruins as the gang makes their way across the countryside in the year following Indonesia’s declaration of independence. Where the film falters is in its rather didactic brand of storytelling, with actors reciting reams of expository dialogue and situations that tend to feel more demonstrative than dramatic.

The pedagogical nature of the filmmaking is evident from the opening scene, which uses a theater piece to depict how the Dutch army showed zero mercy toward Indonesian freedom fighters during the war, labeling them as terrorists and executing them at will. (Estimates of casualties on the Indonesian side range from 100,000 to 250,000, with several million more displaced, versus roughly 15,000 dead on the Dutch side.) Animated sequences are also used to depict the inner thoughts of the film’s hero and narrator, Frans (Nicholas Saputra), a “half-blood” whose mixed Dutch and Indonesian heritage makes him a living, breathing example of the colonial battle that tore his country apart.

entertainment.title: TWS: The Beauty of Growing Up Unscripted
entertainment.summary: With their second single album TO US , SHINYU, DOHOON, YOUNGJAE, HANJIN, JIHOON & KYUNGMIN open up about growing up & embracing imperfections.
entertainment.body:
Since their debut in 2024, TWS have captured the spirit of youth through their signature sound: “Boyhood Pop.” From the excitement of first encounters to the joy of moving forward together, their music has always carried a celebratory energy.

But after more than two years in the spotlight, SHINYU, DOHOON, YOUNGJAE, HANJIN, JIHOON and KYUNGMIN are beginning to see the stories of growing up they’ve long told through their music in a different light.

Their second single album, TO US , which arrived Monday (Nov. 2), turns its attention to the less polished moments along the way. Rather than focusing solely on the highs of youth, TWS now speak more openly about mistakes, regrets, and self-doubt, adding a new layer of complexity through their own experiences. It’s not a rejection of the optimism that has defined their sound, but an expansion of what growing up means to them: recognizing that the moments that didn’t go according to plan have become just as much a part of their story.

In conversation with Billboard Korea , the six members reflect on how they’ve changed since debut, what they’ve learned about themselves and one another, and how they hope to expand their musical identity. When asked what they’d tell their past selves and the group they’ve become, they didn’t talk about setting bigger goals. Instead, they speak of keeping going, taking care of themselves, and growing at their own pace.

For a group that has always found reasons to celebrate through music, TO US offers another: the beauty of embracing who they are, imperfections and all.

What stands out about TO US is how it embraces the mistakes and regrets that come with growing up, rather than treating them as things to hide. Looking back since your debut, is there a moment that felt disappointing at the time, but that you now recognize as something that helped you grow?

JIHOON: When we first debuted, there were so many things I wasn’t as good at as I am now — whether it was my stamina, how I communicated with fans onstage, or my singing and dancing. With each comeback, I’d set small goals for myself, thinking, “I want to do better at this next time.”

But I failed a lot. It hurt when I couldn’t achieve the goals I’d set for myself. Looking back, though, I see those moments as some of the brightest and most precious. They became the motivation to keep working hard, and I think that connects closely with the message of this album.

entertainment.title: With ‘The Girl of Your Dreams,’ Ashe Finds Her Sweet Spot: “I’m A Really Solid Version of Myself”
entertainment.summary: The pop singer's viral hit "Stop The Wedding!" continues to climb the Billboard Hot 100, reaching its highest peak yet this week with the top 25 in sight.
entertainment.body:
Ashe is tucked away in her Nashville home. It’s more of a cottage, she explains, a cup of coffee in hand. It’s straight out of The Holiday.

“It looks like a grandma decorated it,” the singer-songwriter tells The Hollywood Reporter on a recent Zoom call. “But it was in fact me.”

The 33-year-old is in the midst of a career-high. Her latest album, The Girl of Your Dreams, has earned the singer her highest Billboard 200 debut to date, landing at No. 20. The album’s pre-release single “Stop The Wedding!” has continued to climb the charts, landing at its highest-yet position at No. 28. Related Stories News Lenny Kravitz Debunks Viral Rumor That He Died in Horrific Learjet Plane Crash Music Marty Erlichman, Barbra Streisand's Longtime Manager, Dies at 97

It’s not the first time she’s experienced a viral moment — her 2019 single “Moral of the Story,” which was featured in Netflix’s To All The Boys I’ve Loved Before: P.S. I Still Love You , served as a breakout moment for the singer. Heading into the album, she was hopeful that the hype surrounding “Stop The Wedding!” would push people to listen to the entire album, which given its debut this week, it seems that came to fruition.

“‘Stop The Wedding!’ while to the world it stands alone and on its own little island, to me, it’s No. 1 of 11 songs,” she explains. “It lives in a body of work. I’m excited for people to have that context.”

There was a time for Ashe, whose real name is Ashlyn Rae Willson, when she felt extremely protective with her work. There’s always a complicated feeling when sharing an album with the world. But lately, thanks to her latest album and her 2025 stint as The Favors with collaborator Finneas, she’s finding herself moving away from that.

“A previous version of a previous songwriter that I was, was a bit more precious,” she says. “Now, as I’ve gotten older, it’s not that I wouldn’t take it less serious, but it’s art. It’s meant to be interpreted and perceived and misinterpreted.”

Adds Ashe: “I’m very OK with that — probably in a way that I didn’t used to be. I can’t wait for people who love it to love it. And for people that it’s not for, to not get it, and it just to be here.”

entertainment.title: Justin Timberlake to Release 4-Part Docuseries That Includes Janet Jackson as a Guest
entertainment.summary: The project is set to arrive on Apple TV by the end of the year.
entertainment.body:
Justin Timberlake has some things to get off his chest. Variety reported Monday (Nov. 2) that the pop star has a four-part “tell-all” docuseries in the works at Apple TV, featuring none other than Janet Jackson as a guest.

The project is reportedly expected to arrive on the streamer in December, with no further details available at press time aside from one of the discussion topics that will be included. With Miss Jackson onboard, the doc will almost certainly look back on the pair’s infamous 2004 Super Bowl controversy, which involved Timberlake exposing her breast on live TV — aka the incident from which the term “wardrobe malfunction” was born.

The project comes amid a reflective chapter for the former *NSYNC boy bander, who made headlines in 2021 with a public apology to Jackson acknowledging the disparity in how they were respectively treated after the Super Bowl controversy. “I am deeply sorry for the times in my life where my actions contributed to the problem, where I spoke out of turn, or did not speak up for what was right,” Timberlake wrote. “I understand that I fell short in these moments and in many others and benefited from a system that condones misogyny and racism.”

Also in his apology, Timberlake expressed remorse for the disrespectful ways in which he’d previously spoken about Britney Spears following their breakup in 2002.

Things got rocky for JT a few years later in 2024, when he was arrested on suspicion of driving while intoxicated in the Hamptons. He ultimately pleaded guilty to a lesser impaired-driving charge, and the singer was sentenced to 25 hours of community service.

“It’s been a tough week,” Timberlake told fans at one of his Forget Tomorrow World Tour concerts shortly afterward. “I know I’m hard to love sometimes, but you keep loving me right back.”

After the trek ended the following year, the star revealed another challenge he’d been facing behind the scenes: Lyme disease.

“Living with this can be relentlessly debilitating, both mentally and physically,” he wrote in a statement at the time. “When I first got the diagnosis I was shocked for sure. But, at least I could understand why I would be onstage and in a massive amount of nerve pain or, just feeling crazy fatigue or sickness.”

entertainment.title: Bruce Springsteen Backs Michigan’s Dr. Abdul El-Sayed for U.S. Senate Amid Haley Stevens Reversal: ‘He’s a Fighter’
entertainment.summary: "I’m in his corner 100%," the Boss said of the Democratic nominee.
entertainment.body:
Bruce Springsteen has shared his thoughts on the race in Michigan for U.S. Senate, backing Dr. Abdul El-Sayed for the seat as Election Day draws nearer.

In a Monday (Nov. 2) post on Instagram, The Boss shared a statement explaining why he supports the Democratic nominee. “Dr. El-Sayed is a fighter for our American Constitution,” Springsteen wrote. “He’s a fighter for our American Democracy, and he’s a fighter against the corrupt, lawless, and anti-American leadership currently in the White House.”

The endorsement comes amid a close race in Michigan between Dr. El-Sayed and his Republican opponent, Mike Rogers, to take over Democrat Gary Peters’ seat in the Senate. A Democratic win in Michigan is crucial for Democrats as they work to flip the Senate, and recently, Michigan Rep. Haley Stevens threw everyone a curveball by rescinding her support of Dr. El-Sayed and endorsing Rogers. As a result, the state’s Democratic Party chairman Curtis Hertel announced on X that Stevens “is not a current member of the Michigan Democratic Party, nor will she be in the future.”

Springsteen has long been vocal in his political opinions, especially in recent years. He’s repeatedly spoken out against Donald Trump in particular, which has led the president to publicly take aim at the Rock & Roll Hall of Famer a number of times — not that it’s had any success in silencing the Boss.

“I do what I want to do,” Springsteen — who’s topped the Billboard 200 11 times over the course of his career — told Rolling Stone of using his recent Land of Hopes & Dreams trek as a political statement. “This was the show I wanted to make, the story I wanted to tell … I’m sure there were people, and I’ve read things where people were vehement about the content of the show. And that’s just the way the chips fall.”
